# 1. Downloading R and RStudio

Click [here](https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/tp3qv66e75azt9f8o75hp/Getting-Set-Up.pdf?rlkey=x92h6lhit16r9kejn776l0h8o&st=vl7ftwsu&dl=0) for the handout that I share with my students to help them download the software.

# 2. How to use your own datasets in RStudio

After you download the required software, click [here](https://youtu.be/zgzUXn9DArg?si=4Wmh_EOZ-cuLXmTC&t=770) to watch a video tutorial to familiarize yourself with the layout of RStudio and to learn how you can use your own datasets. The tutorial uses a dataset titled, "yrbss2023.csv" in a folder named "QTM 100 Datasets," but you can replace that folder and dataset with your own.

# 3. Posit Academy

[Posit Academy](https://posit.co/products/enterprise/academy/) was very helpful for me to sharpen my R skills. It's a 5-week online training with a 45-minute daily commitment.

# 4. Books

- [R for Data Science](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/)

- [Advanced R](https://adv-r.hadley.nz/)

- [Data Visualization](https://socviz.co/)
